sources.locator: Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58; Section 3.1, printed pages 87-93; Section 5.1, printed pages 123-125; Section 8, Theorem 8.1, printed page 174 (PDF pages = printed pages + 12)

contents.name: Section 2.1 (pp. 55-58): quantum-mechanical observables as self-adjoint operators and their spectral measures
Theorem 3.1 and Theorem 3.2, Section 3.1 (pp. 87-93): the spectral theorem for self-adjoint operators and the bounded functional calculus, with the identity ||P(f)psi||^2 = int |f|^2 d mu_psi
Theorems 5.1-5.2 (pp. 123-125): a self-adjoint operator generates a strongly continuous unitary group; the difference quotient converges exactly on the domain and equals iT
Theorem 5.2 (iii) (pp. 124-125): U(t)D(A)=D(A) and AU(t)=U(t)A; the Schroedinger initial-value problem is solved by the group
Equation (5.4) and the surrounding discussion (p. 124): expectations of the energy are time independent along the flow; this corresponds to conservation of energy
Theorem 5.2 (pp. 123-125) with Lemma 4.9 (p. 126): a vector whose orbit stays in a one-dimensional invariant subspace is a domain eigenvector; commuting groups have commuting generators
Corollary 5.3 (p. 125): a dense U(t)-invariant subspace consists of vectors of essential self-adjointness
contents.reason: Every operator on this page is self-adjoint by hypothesis, so the essential-self-adjointness criterion has no consumer in this pair; it belongs to the later pages that construct model operators from formal differential expressions.

contents.name: Theorem 8.1 (Noether, p. 174): a self-adjoint operator commuting with H has U(t)-invariant domain and conserved expectation values
